{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Doris G. Skillman Stockton''' (1924–2018) was an American mathematician specializing in [[partial differential equation]]s and [[Banach space]]s, and known for her many mathematics textbooks. For many years she was a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].{{r|retires}}

==Education and career==
Stockton entered the [[Douglass Residential College|New Jersey College for Women at Rutgers]] in 1941. Initially planning to study dramatic arts, she was persuaded to switch to mathematics and physics so that she could more directly contribute to the [[World War II]] efforts.{{r|retires}}

She completed her Ph.D. at [[Brown University]] in 1958, with the dissertation ''Singular Parabolic Partial Differential Equations with Time Dependent Coefficients'', supervised by [[Joanne Elliott]].{{r|mgp|brown}}

She joined the faculty at the [[University of Connecticut]] but, soon after, moved to the University of Massachusetts.{{r|ob}} After working for 52 years on the faculty of the University of Massachusetts, Stockton retired in 2006.{{r|retires}}

==Personal life==
Stockton was born on February 9, 1924, in [[New Brunswick, New Jersey]].{{r|ob}}
She was married to Frederick D. Stockton (1920–2015), an associate professor of [[civil engineering]] at the University of Massachusetts.{{r|fredo}}
She died on December 13, 2018, in [[Avon, Connecticut]].{{r|ob}}

==Books==
Stockton was the author of 11 textbooks and workbooks, including:
*''Elements of Mathematics'' (2nd ed., with Helen Murray Roberts, 1956){{r|elm}}
*''Essential Mathematics'' (Scott & Foresman, 1972){{r|esm}}
*''Essential Algebra'' (1973){{r|esa}}
*''Essential Algebra with Functions'' (1973){{r|esaf}}
*''Essential Algebra and Trigonometry'' (Houghton Mifflin, 1978)
*''Essential Precalculus'' (Houghton Mifflin, 1978)
*''Essential College Algebra'' (Houghton Mifflin, 1979)
